title: Off the Map
subtitle: A surveyor hires the company to chart the blank on the map. The dead follow what he takes.
tagline: A surveyor, a blank on the map, and a road the dead still walk. Eight chapters.

map.alt: A hand-drawn map of the March: the mine, the Rain Court, the kilns, the Loadstone and the drowned lock

ending_note: The March is off the map again. Every chapter stays open: play any of them again.

shots.title: Off the Map
shots.text: Every map of the north has a blank in it: forty miles of hills between the Lantern Mine and the river, left empty, with a note in the margin: here we do not go.
Odo Fenn, surveyor, meant to fill it. He hired six of us to walk the old road with him. Half our pay in advance, the rest when the road was on paper.
I kept the company's journal. We set out at first light. Fenn talked about ink and angles all morning, and nobody asked why the blank was blank.

shots.title: Chapter 1 · The Long Haul
shots.text: Day one. The road begins at the Lantern Mine, where haulers once dragged ore up into the light. Fenn wanted the entrance measured before dark. Guy, Curogana and I went in with him.
The haulers are still at work down there. They have not noticed that they are dead. They noticed us.
Fenn sketched the tunnel while Guy cleaned his sword. He never looked at the bodies. “One mark on the map,” he said. “Seven to go.”
That night I asked him what was at the end of the road. “A margin,” he said. I wrote it down, because it sounded like a joke, and he was not a man who joked.

shots.title: Chapter 2 · Rain in the Arcade
shots.text: Day four. The Rain Court: an arcade of grey pillars where the queens of the March once heard petitions. The stories say it has rained there for three hundred years. It was raining when we came.
Someone still holds court. A steward in grave linen sat on the throne, and two shadows stood beside it that fell the wrong way in the light. Guy, Elion and Curogana drew their weapons.
Afterwards the throne was empty except for a bronze seal the size of a palm, four faces around its rim. Elion said to leave it where it lay. We left it.
Fenn was the last of us out of the court. Behind us, for the first time in three hundred years, the rain stopped. Nobody thought much of it. We should have.

shots.title: Chapter 3 · The Draught Shaft
shots.text: Day seven. We slept in the Split Kiln, a brickworks cracked from roof to floor by some old frost. Fenn wanted its chimney for a sightline.
At midnight something climbed up the draught shaft, and then more of it. They went straight for the corner where Fenn slept. Elion, Chruna and I stood in the way.
Chruna said the dead had pushed past her to reach him. “They wanted him,” she said. “Not us. Him.” Fenn said the dead want everybody, and went back to sleep. I did not.

shots.title: Chapter 4 · The Last Wick
shots.text: Day nine. The road goes back under the hills, through the lower galleries of the mine. The old lamps there still burn. As we walked, one by one, they went out behind us.
Under the last lamp a dead knight was waiting, and it spoke, which the dead should not do. “Return what was taken,” it said. Then the dark came down on Elion, Curogana and Chruna.
Elion asked Fenn plainly what he had taken. Fenn showed us his empty hands, his notebook and his ink. “Measurements,” he said. Elion did not believe him. Neither did I. We walked on anyway.

shots.title: Chapter 5 · The Shattered Glaze
shots.text: Day fifteen. Two weeks on the road had made us harder. At the old kiln yard downriver, scavengers had got there first: goblins and kobolds, who follow the dead and strip what they leave behind.
Mara caught one by the collar before the fighting began. It held a scrap of Fenn's map, copied in charcoal. “The thin man drops pages,” it said. “We follow the pages. The dead follow him.”
When it was over, Mara turned out Fenn's coat. The bronze seal fell into the broken glaze. He had taken it from the throne at the Rain Court while we were busy with the dead.

“It is the key to the March,” Fenn said. “Whoever holds it holds the road, and the tomb at the end of it. Four queens’ gold. Your pay ten times over.” Mara said the queens could have their seal back at their own door. The road went there anyway.

shots.title: Chapter 6 · Under the Loadstone
shots.text: Day eighteen. The short way to the river runs beneath the Loadstone, a black rock that tugs at every buckle and blade. The dead of the whole March had gathered under it, waiting for the seal to pass.
They did not wait for us to pass. Elion, Curogana and Chruna went first into the dark.
We came out at dawn above the river, with the old lock half drowned below us. Fenn walked in the middle of us now, and the seal hung wrapped in cloth on Mara's belt. He did not speak all day.

shots.title: Chapter 7 · The Sunken Toll
shots.text: Day twenty. The Sunken Toll: a river lock where the queens of the March took a coin from every boat, and where they were buried when the river rose. Four of them. Sisters.
Mara held up the seal and said we had come to give it back. The four queens rose out of the water. They did not care how it had come.
When the last of them fell, Mara pressed the seal into an empty socket in the toll-house wall. The water went still. Far away, over the hills, it began to rain.
In the morning Fenn was gone, and so was the seal. He had prised it out of the wall while we slept.

shots.title: Chapter 8 · The Last Toll
shots.text: Day twenty-two. We found him back at the Rain Court, on the empty throne, with the seal in his hand. Around him stood the court's old guardians, suits of armour that answer to whoever holds the seal, and the goblin chief who had followed his pages, waiting to be paid.
“Every road has a toll,” Fenn said. “This one is mine.” The armour began to move. Guy, Chruna and I stepped forward.
When the last suit of armour fell, Fenn let go of the seal and ran, and the March let him go. We set the seal back on the throne. In the Rain Court, softly, it began to rain again.
Fenn's map was in the satchel he left behind, finished at last: every gate, every shaft, every lock. I burned it that night, one page at a time.
The March is still a blank on the maps of the north. In the margin there is a note, in my handwriting now: here we do not go. Some places should stay off the map.
